subject: Economics
question_text: Pakistan's GDP measures final goods and services produced within borders. Which is included in Pakistan's GDP but excluded from GNP?
option_a: Remittances from Pakistani workers in Saudi Arabia
option_b: Profit earned by a Chinese-owned factory in Karachi
option_c: Income of a Pakistani doctor in the UK
option_d: Dividends to a Pakistani investor from a Lahore company
explanation_detailed: GDP counts production within borders regardless of ownership. Foreign-owned factory profit adds to GDP but not GNP. Remittances are transfers, not production.

subject: Economics
question_text: When SBP raises the policy rate, the most likely short-run outcome is:
option_a: Banks reduce lending rates, stimulating investment
option_b: Money supply expands as banks borrow cheaply
option_c: Cost of borrowing rises, curbing consumption and investment
explanation_detailed: Higher policy rate raises lending costs — contractionary monetary policy. Capital inflows may strengthen the rupee instead of weakening it.

subject: Economics
question_text: Law of diminishing marginal returns: as more labour is added to fixed land, marginal product eventually:
option_d: Is negative from the first unit
explanation_detailed: Fixed factors become overcrowded; each extra worker adds less output after a point. Core short-run production concept for CSS.

subject: Economics
question_text: Engel's Law: as household income rises, the proportion spent on food tends to:
explanation_detailed: Poorer households spend a larger share on food. Explains consumption differences between rural Pakistan and urban middle class.

subject: Economics
question_text: Which transaction appears on the credit side of Pakistan's current account?
option_b: FDI in a new Faisalabad textile mill
option_c: Export of Sindh rice to Middle East
option_d: SBP purchase of US Treasury bonds
explanation_detailed: Exports are current account credits. Imports are debits; FDI and securities are capital account items.

subject: Economics
question_text: Demand-pull inflation is best described as:
option_a: Rising input costs like electricity tariffs
option_b: Aggregate demand exceeding capacity at full employment
option_c: Decrease in money supply by SBP
explanation_detailed: Too much spending bids up prices economy-wide. Distinguish from cost-push inflation from supply shocks.

subject: Economics
question_text: Opportunity cost of building Dasu Hydropower is:
option_c: Next best alternative forgone (e.g. health/education spending)
option_d: External debt raised for the project
explanation_detailed: Opportunity cost is the best alternative sacrificed — not accounting cost. Central to public finance questions.

subject: Economics
question_text: Ricardo's comparative advantage: trade benefits Pakistan and China even if one is more efficient in all goods, if:
option_b: Each specializes where opportunity cost is relatively lower
explanation_detailed: Trade gains come from relative efficiency, not absolute. Pakistan exports textiles despite productivity gaps.

subject: Economics
question_text: The Laffer Curve shows the relationship between tax rates and:
explanation_detailed: Beyond a point, higher rates reduce revenue by discouraging activity and compliance. Relevant to FBR tax base debates.

subject: Economics
question_text: Best fiscal policy to combat severe recession with rising unemployment:
option_a: Raise taxes and cut development spending
option_c: Increase infrastructure spending and cut certain direct taxes
option_d: Raise policy rate and sell securities
explanation_detailed: Expansionary fiscal policy boosts demand. Option D is monetary policy (SBP), not fiscal.

subject: Physics
question_text: Book on table in Islamabad. Newton's Third Law: force by book on table is:
option_b: Equal and opposite to table on book
option_d: Same direction as gravity on book
explanation_detailed: Action-reaction pairs are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, on different bodies.

subject: Physics
question_text: Copper wire 4 Ω, current 5 A. Potential difference?
explanation_detailed: Ohm's Law V = IR = 5 × 4 = 20 V. High-frequency CSS application.

subject: Physics
question_text: Object 30 cm before concave mirror f=10 cm. Image distance v (real conventions)?
explanation_detailed: u=−30, f=−10 → v=−15 cm: real inverted image 15 cm in front.

subject: Physics
question_text: Bernoulli: increase in fluid speed (constant height) accompanies:
explanation_detailed: Higher kinetic energy per volume → lower pressure at same height. Explains wing lift.

subject: Physics
question_text: Half-life 6 h, start 128 g. Mass after 24 h?

subject: Physics
question_text: Metre rule pivoted at centre. 2 N at 20 cm, 4 N at 80 cm. Torque of 2 N about pivot?
explanation_detailed: 30 cm left of pivot: τ = 2 × 0.30 = 0.6 N·m anticlockwise.

subject: Physics
question_text: Photoelectric effect: increase light intensity (frequency above threshold) will:
option_a: Increase max kinetic energy of photoelectrons
option_c: Increase number of photoelectrons per second
explanation_detailed: K_max depends on frequency (K=hf−φ), not intensity. More photons → more electrons.

subject: Physics
question_text: Radar gun detects higher reflected frequency from approaching car due to:
explanation_detailed: Relative motion compresses wavefronts — higher observed frequency.

subject: Physics
question_text: First Law: 500 J heat in, 200 J work out. ΔU?
explanation_detailed: ΔU = Q − W = 500 − 200 = +300 J. Watch sign conventions.

subject: Physics
question_text: Path difference one wavelength between coherent sources gives:
explanation_detailed: nλ path difference → crest on crest. (n+½)λ → destructive.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Across Period 3 (Na to Cl), atomic radius generally:
explanation_detailed: Same shell, rising nuclear charge pulls electrons closer.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: pH of 0.001 M HCl (complete ionization)?
explanation_detailed: [H+]=10⁻³ → pH=3. Strong acid pH calculation staple.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Zn(s)+Cu²⁺(aq)→Zn²⁺(aq)+Cu(s). Correct redox statement:
explanation_detailed: Zn loses electrons (oxidation). Cu²⁺ gains electrons (reduction).

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Boyle's Law at constant T: pressure and volume are:
explanation_detailed: P₁V₁=P₂V₂. Compression raises collision rate → higher pressure.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Exothermic N₂+3H₂⇌2NH₃+heat. Increase temperature shifts equilibrium:
explanation_detailed: Heat is a product; adding heat shifts left. Haber process uses compromised low T.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Spontaneous galvanic cell: anode and cathode polarity?
explanation_detailed: Electrons leave anode (negative), enter cathode (positive). Opposite in electrolytic cells.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which pair are isotopes?
explanation_detailed: Same element (8 protons), different mass numbers.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Hybridization of central C in CH₄:
explanation_detailed: Four equivalent sigma bonds → tetrahedral sp³ hybridization.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Spontaneous at constant T,P when:
explanation_detailed: ΔG=ΔH−TΔS < 0 defines spontaneity. Enthalpy alone insufficient.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Oxidation state of Fe in [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻:
explanation_detailed: 6 CN⁻ → −6; complex −4 → Fe = +2.
